  - b3_htsteel_process_pool.csv: 34 CANDIDATE samples whose yield strength
    at room temperature (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield
strength at room temperature (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from
the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would prioritize **low-temperature tempering after the 1050°C first heat treatment**, using the closest chromium-steel examples rather than the highest-strength training samples from unrelated alloy families.

The training data support this choice:
- A **13% Cr, 0.12% C** steel treated at 960°C has yield strength **930 MPa after 250°C tempering**, versus **780 MPa after 540°C tempering**.
- Related **13% Cr, 0.30% C** steels tempered at 625–650°C reach approximately **700–720 MPa**. Lower tempering temperatures generally preserve more strength in this family.
- The pool candidates tempered initially at **715–740°C** are therefore less promising than those tempered at 200–450°C. Subsequent thermal exposure does not consistently restore the strength lost during high-temperature tempering.

### Selected candidates

| Rank | Candidate | Step 2 temperature | Basis for selection |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **c021** | 200°C | Low-temperature tempering; 0.20% C with Ni/Mn additions supporting hardenability. |
| 2 | **c015** | 200°C | Nearly tied with c021; similar carbon content and the same principal heat-treatment schedule. |
| 3 | **c017** | 300°C | Same composition as c021, with somewhat greater tempering expected to reduce strength. |
| 4 | **c018** | 300°C | Same composition as c015; likewise expected to retain high strength. |
| 5 | **c006** | 450°C | Best remaining low-tempering-temperature option, narrowly preferred over c014. |

These are **training-informed qualitative predictions**, not measured strengths. The ordering within each 200°C or 300°C pair is uncertain; **c014** is also a close alternative for fifth place.

Final: c021, c015, c017, c018, c006
